newsitem.title: USA: FAA releases draft report for Lambert expansion.
newsitem.headline: FAA releases draft report for Lambert expansion.

text.p: The Federal Aviation Administration on Thursday released a draft environmental impact statement for a planned $1.87 billion expansion of Lambert-St. Louis International Airport.
St. Louis officials heralded the release as a big step forward in their plans to expand the airport to meet growing aviation needs.
Mayor Freeman Bosley Jr called the draft statement "a huge milestone," adding that he was "very confident that any remaining obstacles to complete the final expansion plan will be overcome."
Colonel Leonard Griggs Jr, Lambert's director, said the draft statement supports the airport's plan to build a new runway and make terminal and other improvements.

Because of a shrinking avialability of federal aviation fund dollars, Griggs said the $1.87 billion project would largely be financed with general airport revenue bonds. He added that the airport is also considering the issuance of bonds backed only by passenger facility charge revenues in the wake of recent rating agency acceptance of such debt.
A spokeswoman for the FAA's southern region said a public hearing will be held Oct. 28 on the draft report and that a final report by the FAA is due out around the beginning of next year.
In a statement, TWA, the St. Louis-based carrier, said the draft statement "does not contain any surprises and clearly shows the only viable options to expand."
